purpose: Doxycycline is an antibiotic used to treat a wide variety of bacterial infections, including chest infections, skin infections like acne, urinary tract infections, and sexually transmitted infections like chlamydia. It is also used to prevent malaria when traveling to certain areas. Your doctor may prescribe it for other conditions as well, such as Lyme disease or certain eye infections.
how_it_works: Doxycycline works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply. Without these proteins, the bacteria cannot survive, and your immune system can clear the infection. It does not work against viral infections like colds or the flu.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, and diarrhea. You may also notice heartburn or a sore throat if the pill gets stuck in your esophagus. Some people experience increased sensitivity to sunlight, which can cause you to sunburn more easily than usual.
warnings: Always take doxycycline with a full glass of water and stay upright for at least 30 minutes afterward to protect your esophagus. Avoid lying down right after taking it. Do not take it with dairy products, antacids, or iron supplements as these can reduce how well the medication works. This medication can make birth control pills less effective, so talk to your doctor about backup contraception. Do not use it if you are pregnant or in children under 8 years old, as it can affect bone and tooth development. Stay out of direct sunlight and use sunscreen while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The typical adult dose is 100 mg taken twice a day, or sometimes 200 mg once a day, depending on what is being treated. For acne, a lower dose of 40 mg once daily may be used. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and finish the entire course, even if you start feeling better early.
